review.reason_for_change: Anthropic explicitly disabled Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all customers, directly engaging stakeholder communication during model deactivation. The public statement gives the attributed directive, scope and alternatives; it does not preserve the maintained communication plan, contact provisions and complete affected-stakeholder coverage. That full planning proposition remains Boundary despite the observed disclosure. The result does not adjudicate the undisclosed directive or infer formal framework adoption.

conclusion_change.previous: The source identifies a concrete infrastructure authority projection. The government directive targeted foreign nationals, including people outside the United States; Anthropic then removed Fable 5 and Mythos 5 from all customers to comply. A sovereign access restriction thus became a broader rule of availability through a globally relied-upon provider. VIGIL maps this operational scope expansion to Jurisdiction-Bounded Infrastructure Authority at medium confidence. The classification concerns the infrastructure-mediated effect on users beyond the targeted cohort, not a finding that the government lacked legal power over foreign nationals, that Anthropic acted unlawfully, or that a less restrictive technical implementation was immediately feasible. The undisclosed order and compliance architecture limit stronger causal and legal conclusions. The retained jurisdiction-bounded infrastructure failure is a bounded operational scope-projection finding at medium confidence, alongside successful disclosure of which models remained available. It does not determine the directive’s legal reach, provider liability or technical feasibility of narrower compliance. No source-grounded canonical export-control requirement is independently available from the undisclosed order. The selected NIST deactivation communication and SDOS degradation candidates retain unresolved adopted-scope and trigger/plan evidence, without external findings.
